chunks: Ibn Muskan narrated from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a muhrim who intends to do an act, and his companions say to him, “By Allah, do not do it,” and he says, “By Allah, I will surely do it,” and they exchange oaths repeatedly. Does there become binding upon him what is binding upon the one guilty of disputation?
He عليه السلام said: “No. He only intended by this to honor his brother. What only becomes binding upon him is that which was disobedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.”

key_terms.أَصْحَابُهُ: his companions or associates present with him
key_terms.إِكْرَامَ أَخِيهِ: honoring his brother in social interaction
key_terms.فَيُحَالِفُهُ: he exchanges oaths with him repeatedly
key_terms.مَعْصِيَةً: an act of disobedience to Allah
key_terms.ٱلْجِدَالِ: the prohibited disputation or contentious oath-taking in ihram
key_terms.ٱلْمُحْرِمِ: a person in the state of ihram during hajj or ʿumrah

ai.seo_question: Does repeating “By Allah” during ihram count as jidal and incur its penalty?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that repeated oath-taking by a muhrim in ordinary interaction with companions does not automatically count as the prohibited jidal of ihram. The ruling depends on whether the speech amounts to disobedience to Allah, not merely on the presence of emphatic oath language. It also indicates consideration of intention, such as honoring one's fellow believer.
